goals: Mechanistic: resolve how water partitioning (snow accumulation/melt, ET, runoff, recharge) varies across the Upper Yakima elevation gradient and its dominant soils
Validation: compare simulated peak SWE against in-basin SNOTEL observations across elevation bands

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM resolves the vertical water/energy/snow balance; NLDAS-2 forcing provides orographically varying precip/temperature across the ~1900 m relief, so an elevation-stratified column set carries a real (12-km-smoothed) elevation-climate signal.

answerable: Elevation control on snowpack and partitioning via NLDAS-2 orographic forcing variation (12-km resolution)
Soil-texture control on partitioning via per-column SSURGO

not_answerable.why: Single-column runs are independent 1-D points with no lateral routing, so there is no native integrated basin streamflow to compare to a gauge

not_answerable.aspect: Sub-12 km terrain, aspect, and valley/ridge microclimate effects on snow
not_answerable.why: NLDAS-2 at ~12 km cannot resolve within-cell lapse rate; ridgetop SWE will be underestimated

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation bands x dominant soils) with light replication at the sensitive transition
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 5 elevation bands span the 500-2400 m gradient and bracket the rain-snow transition; crossing with 2 dominant soils = 10 columns to separate elevation-climate from soil effects, +2 replicate columns in the 1200-1600 m transition band where snow-fraction and partitioning are most sensitive.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate columns in the mid-elevation rain-snow transition (1200-1600 m) where snow-vs-rain sensitivity and melt-timing are greatest; ensure each band's columns sit in distinct NLDAS cells so the orographic forcing signal is real; oversample valley-adjacent positions for recharge relevance.
sampling_strategy.replication: 2 replicate columns in the transition band on the two dominant soils to check soil vs elevation attribution where the signal is strongest

sampling_plan.reason: Rain-dominated baseline: partitioning with little/no persistent snowpack, contrasts against snow bands.
Lower edge of intermittent snow; captures onset of snow influence on melt and recharge timing.

sampling_plan.group: rain-snow transition 1200-1600 m x 2 soils + replication
sampling_plan.reason: Most climate-sensitive band; replicated on both soils to separate elevation-climate from soil control on snow and partitioning.
Seasonal snowpack dominant; resolves melt-driven runoff and recharge peak.
Deepest/longest snowpack; anchors the cold end of the gradient and SNOTEL comparison (expect ridgetop underestimation).

validation_design.comparison: co-located — place a validation column at each in-basin SNOTEL site and compare simulated annual peak SWE and melt-out timing; expect ridgetop underestimation from 12-km averaging
validation_design.metric: bias and RMSE on peak SWE; date offset on melt-out
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on number of SNOTEL sites within HUC 17030001

validation_design.comparison: aggregated — NOT feasible without routing; flagged as a gap, single columns produce no integrated streamflow

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 forcing (baseline period), native SSURGO soil per column, WTD-informed warm start + short spin-up

requires_capabilities.capability: SNOTEL site locator / ingest for HUC 17030001
requires_capabilities.why: Validation columns must be pinned to actual SNOTEL coordinates in-basin
requires_capabilities.blocks: co-located SWE validation and its column count

requires_capabilities.why: Single columns produce no integrated streamflow
NLDAS-2 12-km cells cannot resolve within-cell lapse rate/aspect
requires_capabilities.blocks: accurate ridgetop SWE and fine-scale elevation signal

requires_capabilities.why: Assign columns to elevation bands and confirm distinct NLDAS cells
Identify dominant soil groups per elevation band

requires_capabilities.capability: multi-year spin-up / Fan-2013 WTD warm start
requires_capabilities.why: Recharge and water-table states are cold-start artifacts otherwise

assumptions: Basin lies within CONUS so NLDAS-2 orographic forcing applies across the elevation gradient
At least two distinct dominant SSURGO soil groups exist across the bands (to be confirmed by soil sampling)
Selected columns in each band fall in distinct NLDAS cells so elevation-climate variation is real, not duplicated
open_questions: How many SNOTEL sites lie within HUC 17030001, and at what elevations?
Is a routing/aggregation capability planned, or should USGS-gauge validation be dropped from scope?
Preferred forcing period (full 1980-2018 climatology vs. a shorter representative window given ~30 min/yr/column NLDAS cost)?
